question: The circumference of the base of the cylindrical vessel is 154 cm and its height is 49 mm. How many litres of water can it hold? (correct to three places of decimals, use π = 22/7)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Base Circumference = 2πr = 154 ⇒ r = 154 × (7/44) = 24.5 cm.

Height = 49 mm = 4.9 cm.

Volume (cm³) = πr²h = (22/7) × 24.5² × 4.9 = 9243.85 cm³.

Capacity in Litres = 9243.85 ÷ 1000 = 9.24385 Litres ≈ 9.244 Litres.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.244 Litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Circumference of the base = 154 cm

Height of the cylinder (h) = 49 mm = 4.9 cm

**Formula Used:**

Circumference of a circle = 2πr

Volume of a cylinder = πr²h

1 Litre = 1000 cm³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c136fce426f15477da0401ffe2ae40481d787b3e38508c49dd7a63365bd5dce8.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 154

⇒ (44/7) × r = 154

⇒ r = (154 × 7) ÷ 44

⇒ r = 24.5 cm

⇒ Volume of the vessel = (22/7) × (24.5)² × 4.9

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 600.25 × 4.9

⇒ Volume = 22 × 600.25 × 0.7

⇒ Volume = 9243.85 cm³

Since 1000 cm³ = 1 Litre:

⇒ Capacity in Litres = 9243.85 ÷ 1000 = 9.24385 Litres

⇒ Correct to three places of decimals ≈ 9.244 Litres

**∴ The correct answer is 9.244 Litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume and Surface Area of a Cylinder

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh | Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr(r + h) | Volume = πr²h

Liquid Capacity Conversions

1 m³ = 1000 Litres | 1 Litre = 1000 cm³ | 1 cm³ = 1 millilitre (ml)
